items.title: [Dreaming3D Inc - News] Saturn 4 Ultra 16K LCD Connection Error: Cable, Firmware, Screen or Mainboard? How to Tell, and What to Buy
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

&&&

Repair guide · Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K · Updated November 20, 2026

Saturn 4 Ultra 16K LCD Connection Error: Cable, Firmware, Screen or Mainboard? How to Tell, and What to Buy

The self-check flags the LCD screen connection. Before you buy a screen, rule out the ribbon cable and the firmware, which take seven screws to check instead of fifty-eight.

Your Saturn 4 Ultra 16K boots, runs its self-check, and one line comes back failed: the LCD screen connection. The screen is the expensive, obvious suspect, and Elegoo will sell you a new one for $129.99. But the same message can come from a ribbon cable that has slipped in its latch, or from firmware that doesn’t match your mainboard. You can check both with the back cover off, which is 7 screws. Getting a new screen in takes 58.

We print customer jobs on a Saturn 4 Ultra 16K in our San Diego shop, and we repair Elegoo resin printers in person around San Diego County. This guide takes Elegoo’s own procedures and puts them in the order we’d work through them, cheapest first. It also covers the parts, part numbers and warranty terms as they stood on November 20, 2026.

The short version

  • What it means: the mainboard isn’t getting the answer it expects from the 10-inch exposure screen under the vat. There are four suspects: the ribbon cable, firmware that doesn’t match the board, the screen itself, and the mainboard.
  • Check in order of screws: 0 (power-cycle, firmware version, exposure-test photo), 7 (board revision, firmware match, reseat the ribbon at the board), 48 (the ribbon at the screen) and 58 (a new screen).
  • 16K parts are not 12K parts: the 16K screen (A0S0V1, $129.99), mainboard (A0S061) and firmware are their own. The Saturn 4 Ultra screen ($114.99) and its firmware file don’t belong in a 16K.
  • Warranty: Elegoo covers the screen for 3 months and the machine for 12, counted from when your order arrived. Leaks and third-party repairs are excluded. If you’re inside either window, email Elegoo before you open the printer.
  • Local help: in San Diego County we can do every step on-site. Los Angeles visits are by appointment. Anywhere else, we can walk you through it over video.

Three things people get wrong about this error

“An LCD error means the screen is dead.”
Not necessarily. Elegoo’s own LCD display guide lists a badly seated or damaged ribbon cable and outdated or incompatible firmware as causes, alongside a failed screen. It has you reseat the cable at both ends and update the firmware before contacting support.
“Saturn 4 Ultra parts fit the 16K.”
Some do. Elegoo sells the same build plate and release film for the Saturn 4, 4 Ultra and 4 Ultra 16K. The screen, mainboard and firmware are different. Elegoo sells a separate 16K screen and publishes separate 16K firmware, and Printer Hub reports that 12K firmware makes a 16K stop recognizing its screen.
“Elegoo’s wiki has a fix for this.”
Not a specific one. On November 20, 2026, Elegoo’s 16K wiki page listed five self-test error guides: resin tank, X-axis motor, auto-leveling, foreign matter and mechanical sensor. None covers the LCD line. The nearest official procedure is the general LCD Screen Display Issue page, which covers all of Elegoo’s LCD printers.

What the self-check is actually telling you

At power-on, and whenever you run it by hand, the 16K checks its hardware and lists each item with a status. Printer Hub’s reference table names the line “Status of LCD screen connection”; the exact wording can vary between firmware versions. Elegoo’s manual says only that the printer checks key hardware at startup, and that you should follow the on-screen prompts and not touch the machine while it runs.

The 16K has two screens. One is the touch screen you tap. The other is the 10-inch, 15120 × 6230 mono LCD under the vat, which masks the UV light into each layer. This error is about the second one. If the touch screen is stuck on the ELEGOO logo, that is a different fault, and Elegoo has a separate guide for it that blames firmware corruption or a short circuit.

Read the symptom before you pick up a hex key

What you see Most likely Start here
LCD line fails right after a firmware update Firmware that doesn’t match your mainboard revision Device Information (0 screws), then the capacitor check (7 screws)
LCD line fails after the printer was moved, shipped or opened for another repair Ribbon lifted or crooked in its latch Reseat it at the mainboard (7 screws)
LCD line fails right after a new screen went in Ribbon not fully seated or latched at one end Reopen and seat both ends; check any end markings
LCD line fails after a resin leak Resin on or in the screen or a connector Stop powering it on; read our resin leak guide
Self-check passes and the exposure test shows the image, but nothing cures Not this fault: the UV light path Elegoo’s UV light guide; the adapter should read 24 V, 6 A
Exposure test shows part of the image, lines or dead pixels The screen, or a damaged cable Photograph it; our Saturn 4 Ultra errors guide covers dead pixels
Touch screen stuck on the ELEGOO logo Firmware corruption or a short, not the LCD line Elegoo’s recovery firmware steps

One trap worth knowing: Elegoo says the 16K needs a 24 V, 6 A adapter, and that a 12 V Mercury wash-and-cure adapter plugged in by mistake stops the UV light from working. If both bricks share your bench, read the label.

1Check before you open anything (0 screws)

These cost nothing and tell you which branch you’re on.

  1. Power-cycle and watch the check. Turn it off at the switch, wait, turn it on, and let the self-check run without touching the printer. Note whether the LCD line fails every time or only some of the time.
  2. Write down when it started. After a firmware update, a move, a leak or a screen swap? The table above points each one at a different first step.
  3. Read the firmware version. Go to Touch Screen > Device Information and note whether the version ends in the letter B. You need this at the next step.
  4. Run the exposure test and photograph it. Take out the vat and plate, run Tool > Screen Exposure (some Elegoo pages call it Tool > Exposure) with the ELEGOO pattern, and photograph the screen. Is it blank, partial or normal? Elegoo support asks for a photo of the screen not exposing and one during exposure.
  5. Find your order number. If you bought from a distributor, find the invoice instead. Elegoo asks for one or the other.

Wear nitrile gloves whenever the vat is out. Uncured resin is a skin irritant, and resin on your fingers ends up on ribbon contacts.

2Check behind the back cover (7 screws)

Power off and unplug the adapter. Take out the 7 screws on the rear cover with a 2.0 mm Allen key. That exposes the mainboard and the mainboard end of the LCD ribbon.

  1. Identify the board revision. Elegoo’s X-axis self-test guide has you check whether a capacitor is fitted to the mainboard. Printer Hub describes a pair on the right side of the board. Take a sharp photo of the whole board: Elegoo asks for one, and the right firmware file depends on it.
  2. Match the firmware to the board. See the firmware panel below. A board with the capacitor needs firmware ending in B, installed from a USB drive. A board without it updates over the air.
  3. Reseat the ribbon at the mainboard. Peel off the tape over the ribbon, lift the latch and slide the cable out. Look for creases, tears, scorch marks or resin on the contacts. Slide it back in straight and all the way, press the latch down, and tape it again. Elegoo’s guide for its sibling Jupiter 2 asks for the cable to sit parallel to the latch. On cables with marked ends, the end marked LCD or SCREEN faces the screen and the end marked MB faces the mainboard.
  4. Close up and retest. Refit the back cover with all 7 screws. Elegoo’s reassembly step mentions only five; put back what you took out. Power on, then rerun the self-check and the exposure test.

Firmware: match it to the board

What you find What to do
Capacitor fitted, version ends in B Nothing to change. The firmware matches, so move on to the ribbon.
Capacitor fitted, version doesn’t end in B Update from a USB drive with Elegoo’s B file for the 16K: Saturn 4 Ultra 16K Firmware-V1.4.4B-20251023-V8. Elegoo’s page lists the 12K file, Saturn 4 Ultra Firmware-V1.4.5B-20251028-V4, on the next line. Don’t grab that one.
No capacitor Update over the air. Elegoo’s download center has no firmware file for the 16K and recommends OTA.
Won’t boot after an update Use Elegoo’s recovery file, ChituUpgrade.bin, in the root folder of a FAT32 USB drive smaller than 16 GB, then update again.

Never load Saturn 4 Ultra (12K) firmware on a 16K. Printer Hub reports that the printer then stops recognizing its screen, which produces exactly the error you’re trying to fix.

Stop here if a connector looks scorched or has resin on it. Photograph it, leave the printer off, and contact Elegoo or a repair shop. Powering a contaminated board can turn a cable job into a mainboard job.

3Reach the screen end of the ribbon (48 screws)

Elegoo’s general guide says to check the cable at the screen as well as at the board. On the 16K, the only route Elegoo documents to that end is its LCD replacement procedure. The screen’s circuit board comes within reach once the base is off, which is screw 48 by our count: back cover 7, UV housing 7, cover tops 10, cover bottoms 10, base 14. On the way you unplug the touch screen ribbon, the camera, the LED, the Wi-Fi antenna and the UV board plugs, and you cut the cable ties.

So this is where you decide whether to keep going yourself:

  • Still inside Elegoo’s window? That’s 12 months for the machine and 3 for the screen. Email 3dp@elegoo.com with the evidence listed in the warranty section before you go further. Elegoo’s policy excludes printers repaired by a third party or modified by the owner.
  • Out of warranty and comfortable with ribbon latches? Carry on. Have fresh tape and cable ties ready, because you’ll cut the old ties.
  • Not comfortable? This is a sensible place to hand it off. See the local help section below.

Elegoo asks for a photo of the QR code on the screen, and its policy excludes LCD screens without an identifiable serial number. Don’t peel or scratch that label, on the old screen or the new one.

4Replace the screen (58 screws, $129.99)

Replace the screen if the exposure test is still blank or partial after you’ve reseated both ends of the ribbon and matched the firmware, or if you can see cracks, lines or dead pixels.

  1. Back of the printer. Power off and unplug. Take off the back cover (7 screws, 2.0 mm). Free the LCD ribbon at the mainboard. Unplug the LED and camera plugs, and pull the Wi-Fi antenna with tweezers.
  2. UV housing. Lift the UV enclosure and raise the camera slightly. Take out the 6 screws under the housing assembly and the 1 at its back (2.5 mm), then lift it away.
  3. Side and front covers. Remove the 10 screws along the edge of the middle panel. Then remove the bottom screws of the right (3), left (3) and front (4) covers. Open the front cover gently, because the touch screen ribbon is still attached. Untape and unlatch it.
  4. Base. Cut the cable ties, unplug the UV light board and mainboard plugs, and remove the base (14 screws).
  5. Old screen out. Peel the tape along the screen’s edge and cut the ties on its circuit board. Remove the Fresnel lens (10 screws) without touching its surface. Push the screen forward out of the middle panel and clean the old double-sided tape off the frame.
  6. New screen in. Fit the new ribbon to the screen’s board, latch it and tape it. Put double-sided tape on the lower frame and peel the protective films. Seat the screen glass side down, hold the X-axis while you press the edges, then tape the edge.
  7. Everything else back. Refit the Fresnel lens (10), the ties on the screen’s board, the base (14), the side and front covers, the touch screen ribbon, the housing assembly, the plugs and the back cover.
  8. Verify. Power on and run Tool > Exposure > ELEGOO. The logo should show cleanly. If the LCD line still fails, the first suspect is the ribbon you just seated.

That’s Elegoo’s sequence, shortened. Watch Elegoo’s video and keep its page open while you work. It shows which plug is which better than any description.

5When it’s the mainboard

Suspect the board last. That means a known-good screen and a good, properly seated ribbon still fail the check, with firmware that matches the board. Elegoo publishes no test that isolates the board for this line, so in practice the proof is substitution: the fault stays when everything around the board has been swapped or ruled out. Elegoo does publish a general board-health check in its stuck-on-logo guide. With every cable except the touch screen ribbon unplugged, a printer that still can’t reach the main menu probably has a faulty board.

The 16K board is A0S061. Printer Hub gives the Saturn 4 Ultra (12K) board as A0S071. On November 20, 2026, Elegoo US’s Saturn parts page listed 21 products: screens, build plates, release film and so on. It had no 16K mainboard and no separate LCD ribbon cable. Ask Elegoo support for the board, and send the board photo so they match the revision.

Elegoo’s motherboard procedure goes in from the back and the right side. Common questions about this error

What does the LCD screen connection failure in the Saturn 4 Ultra 16K self-test mean?

It means the mainboard isn’t getting the response it expects from the 10-inch exposure screen under the vat. The usual suspects are the LCD ribbon cable, firmware that doesn’t match the mainboard revision, the screen itself, and, last on the list, the mainboard. It isn’t about the touch screen you tap.

Does the LCD connection error mean my screen is dead?

Not necessarily. Elegoo’s own LCD display guide lists the ribbon cable and outdated or incompatible firmware as causes and has you reseat the cable and update firmware before contacting support. Check Device Information to see whether the version ends in B, then take off the back cover and check whether a capacitor is fitted to the mainboard. Developer Cody Collier has released NO SPEAKER, a free, open-source tool that makes a MacBook’s Force Touch trackpad produce speech, tones and simple music through its haptic motor, even with the laptop’s speakers muted. The software drives the motor fast enough to make the glass surface vibrate audibly. It cannot play sound from other apps, and its output is quiet and robotic. NO SPEAKER uses a private, undocumented macOS framework to control the motor, so an Apple software update could break compatibility. The project is available on GitHub; Collier has tested it on only a small number of Mac models.

items.title: [Fast Company] All these outages show how corporate America needs to modernize out-of-date tech
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Over the past five days, a string of high-profile tech outages has left Americans struggling to send emails, catch flights, and access their bank accounts.

While the disruptions raised concerns about AI-powered cybersecurity threats, the real culprit may be something less sinister: corporate America’s tech systems are simply out of date. 

Outages like those at JPMorgan Chase, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), and Microsoft can occur when computer systems are undergoing major upgrades, Marva Bailer, CEO of tech advisory firm Qualaix, told the New York Post. Bolting on new technology can leave the systems vulnerable.

Although it is unclear whether the recent outages were directly related to artificial intelligence, many organizations are currently upgrading their networks to handle AI tools. Microsoft attributed its outage to an issue that arose during a network capacity upgrade, according to the Financial Times.

The time of year could also be a factor, as technicians rush to make sure systems are ready for the holiday shopping and travel season.

“It’s holiday time, it’s travel time, it’s shopping,” Bailer told the New York Post. “So, you have all those higher spikes in volume and more pressure to [update your systems].”

AI is also allowing companies to identify software vulnerabilities far more quickly, possibly leaving IT workers with too much work on their hands, the Post reported.

Like Bailer, U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin attributed the disruptions to companies trying to upgrade aging systems, during an appearance on CNBC earlier today.

“[They’re] pushing new technology on top of really old computer systems, and it just seems to overwhelm the system,” he said.

The disruptions serve as a reminder of how cutting-edge technology is often still dependent on centralized, aging systems.

Friday’s nationwide ground stop, which resulted in more than 18,000 flight cancellations over three days, was triggered by the installation of a single router at a remote facility in Arkansas, Reuters reported. Monday’s software glitch at JPMorgan Chase disrupted transactions for customers of other major banks, even though their own computer systems were functioning normally.

Indeed, third-party tech providers have accounted for roughly two-thirds of publicly reported IT outages over the past nine years, according to a recent report from Uptime Institute, a global digital infrastructure advisory firm based in New York City.

items.content_html:

Oregon State University researchers grew potatoes through their full life cycle in simulated lunar regolith after adding organic matter; a mixture containing 30% vermicompost produced yields comparable to those in terrestrial soil. The NASA-funded experiment took place in a greenhouse on Earth and used simulated material, not material collected on the moon, so it does not establish that crops can be grown on the lunar surface. The trial used five regolith simulants and the Modoc potato variety. Researchers plan to test 10 more potato varieties and are studying growth in larger pots; the first trial’s small pots produced small tubers.

items.title: [space.com] Apollo 12 lightning strikes prompted NASA to tighten launch weather rules
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Lightning struck NASA’s Apollo 12 Saturn V rocket twice within seconds of its Nov. 14, 1969, launch, disrupting spacecraft telemetry and endangering the mission. Mission Control engineer John Aaron recognized the readings from an earlier test and recommended switching the Signal Conditioning Equipment to its auxiliary setting, which restored the data. Investigators concluded the rocket and its conductive exhaust plume had triggered a discharge in an electrically charged part of the atmosphere, even though no active thunderstorm lay along the immediate flight path. NASA expanded launch weather restrictions to account for atmospheric electrical conditions, not only visible lightning and thunderstorms.

A World Weather Attribution study published Friday found that a strong El Niño drove Indonesia’s severe rainfall shortfall this year, while human-caused climate change made temperatures during the August-to-October fire season about 1.6 degrees Celsius higher. Researchers said warming made hot, dry fire conditions about three times more likely, while El Niño cut seasonal rainfall by roughly half. Decades of deforestation and peatland drainage also left the landscape more vulnerable to ignition. The fires have spread hazardous haze across Indonesia and neighboring Southeast Asian countries. Nusantara Atlas, an independent monitoring platform, estimated that fires affected 2.88 million hectares from January through October. The Indonesian government had not confirmed that total or issued its own estimate. Researchers called for peatland restoration, stronger land protections and reduced fossil-fuel emissions. Fires were still burning, with smoke detected in eastern Kalimantan on Nov. 12.

items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

France summoned Iran’s ambassador on Nov. 10 and said it would seek European Union sanctions and consider other responses to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration systems that Paris attributes to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard. The October operation affected about 700 French retail sites. Tehran has denied responsibility. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Paris would take measures it considered proportionate to deter further attacks, including steps it would not disclose publicly. The Paris prosecutor’s office opened a judicial investigation into the Shahid Kaveh cyber unit and requested international arrest warrants for its leader and two deputies. Iran’s Foreign Ministry called the accusation baseless and one-sided, while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused France of shifting blame. The EU said it was ready to coordinate a response with member states. Foreign ministers are due to discuss the issue on Nov. 16.

items.title: [aawsat.com] Jaramana car bombing prompts searches in Druze-majority Damascus suburb
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Security teams in Jaramana searched vehicles and checked surveillance cameras after a car bomb struck a residential area near al-Naseem garage, damaging nearby cars and buildings, according to reports. The blast on Saturday, Nov. 14, killed a man and a girl, according to medical sources cited by Asharq Al-Awsat and Al Jazeera. Reports differed on the number of wounded: Syria’s state television said two people were wounded, while the Interior Ministry reported one. The explosion occurred near a battery-production site in Jaramana, a Damascus suburb with a large Druze community. Syria’s Internal Security Forces cordoned off the area and opened an investigation. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights said accounts differed over the blast’s precise location and nature, and verification was continuing. Residents told Asharq Al-Awsat they heard the blast at about 8 p.m. and saw the car burning. Security vehicles arrived within minutes, and streets leading to the site were closed, with access allowed for ambulances and civil defense crews.
